questions.q: What does a Contact object represent?
options: An individual person, typically related to an Account
A company or organization
A support ticket
A marketing initiative
questions.explain: Contact represents one specific person, usually linked to the Account for the company they work at.

questions.q: How is a Contact typically connected to a company in Salesforce?
options: Through the Contact's Account Name field, linking it to the related Account
Contacts cannot be connected to Accounts at all
Through the Lead Source field
Through Contact Roles only, with no direct Account link
questions.explain: The Account Name field on a Contact record links it to the company Account it belongs to.

questions.q: What is the real difference between a Lead and a Contact, per this lesson?
options: A Lead is a person before qualification/Account connection; a Contact is a person after that connection is established
There is no difference — Lead and Contact are the same object with two different names
A Contact is always a company, while a Lead is always a person
A Lead can never become a Contact
questions.explain: Lead and Contact represent sequential stages of the same relationship, bridged by Lead Conversion.

questions.q: What does a Contact Role record on an Opportunity?
options: Not just that a Contact is associated with the deal, but what role they play in it (e.g. Decision Maker)
The Contact's home address
The Contact's Lead Source
Whether the Contact is a Business Account or Person Account
questions.explain: Contact Role captures the specific role a person plays on a deal, such as Decision Maker, Influencer, or Economic Buyer.

questions.q: To find "who are the decision makers across our open pipeline," what relationship path does an analyst need to traverse?
options: Opportunity through Contact Role to Contact
Lead directly to Case
Account directly to Campaign
Contact directly to Lead, with no other objects involved
questions.explain: This requires a three-object traversal: Opportunity to Contact Role to Contact, not a single direct link.
